leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part prize on B019 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and the citations differ only in wording. Members share the view that the proglucagon-to-drug chain is unusually complete, independently confirmed in large outcome trials and timely. What is not shared is the treatment of Knudsen. Some members would keep her out and acknowledge drug development in the citation. Some would make her the natural replacement if Mojsov's priority weakens. Wahren-Herlenius raised her as arguably as decisive for patients as the physiology. Members also differ on how serious the Mojsov and Habener question is, and on whether B019 should stand alone or share the prize with a second part.

areas_of_agreement: All six members rank B019 first and propose the same three laureates, Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, in their preferred configuration.
All six describe the main reservation about B019 as attribution (Mojsov versus Habener, and Knudsen excluded by the three-person cap), not scientific merit or maturity.
B030 is listed as an alternative by all six members, B012 by three (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Svenningsson) and B040 by three (Perlmann, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius).
Several members say that B012 faces a six-name allocation problem that no trio resolves cleanly, with Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenboeck left out of any three.

Several members say that B024 is early because no therapy has yet come from it and credit within the Chen laboratory is unsettled. Linnarsson and Sandberg said the same of CAR-T attribution or readiness, noting Eshhar's absence.
scientific_disputes: Whether a mechanistic discovery without an approved therapy, such as B040 (unfolded protein response), is competitive with therapy-linked candidates. Perlmann would rank it higher, while Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius see its disease link as mostly mechanistic.

Whether an enabling research tool such as B012 fits a Medicine prize. Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius stress limited clinical translation (early retinal cases), while Linnarsson, El-Manira and Svenningsson say causal circuit control has changed experimental physiology and that category alone is no bar.

Whether the prize should reward basic hormone discovery, drug design, or both. Members disagree about whether medicinal chemistry for long-acting analogues is a separate recognition or part of the scientific core.
Long-term safety and durability of incretin therapy, including effects in pregnancy and in young patients, are noted as still accumulating, though no one says they alter the core discovery.
attribution_disputes: B019: Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36/37) form against Habener's group, who are not among the credited names. Several members state they cannot verify the history from the supplied record.

B019: Knudsen is outside the three-person cap. Linnarsson would substitute her for Mojsov only if the record weakens Mojsov's claim, and Wahren-Herlenius raised Knudsen in her opening proposal. El-Manira notes that the third place is a real choice between Mojsov and Knudsen, and also names a Holst and Drucker pair as a fallback.
B012: six credited names for three places. El-Manira and Linnarsson favour Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann. Sandberg points to Boyden's and Bamberg's priority claims as a core dispute.

B030: whether the achievement is CAR engineering (June, Sadelain) or cell therapy more broadly (adding Rosenberg), and how Eshhar's original chimeric-receptor concept and first-generation clinical teams are handled.

B040: Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius treat Walter and Mori as a clean pair, but El-Manira notes that Ron and Kaufman's PERK and ATF6 contributions complicate the claim. Wahren-Herlenius notes that integrated stress response work is outside the ballot.

B027 (TOR): Svenningsson and Sandberg disagree on whether Hall with Schreiber or with Sabatini is the better pair, and Perlmann would give Hall alone the clearest attribution. Members say others outside the credited list, such as Brown and Sabers, also have claims.
B024: members who comment would limit credit to Chen and Barber, but the roles of Ishikawa, Sun and Wu as trainees remain open.
maturity_disputes: B019 is described by all six as mature, independently confirmed and timely, and Sandberg calls it arguably overdue.
B012: clinical validation is limited to early retinal work, which Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius weigh more heavily than Linnarsson does.
B040: confirmed over about three decades, but with disease relevance still mostly implied and no therapy.
B024: Sandberg judges it one to two cycles early, and Linnarsson and Svenningsson cite the lack of an approved therapy.
B030: strong haematologic clinical proof, with late toxicities, secondary malignancies and limited solid-tumour effect noted as open.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) and Perlmann disclose co-authored work on dopamine-neuron topics. Both state that it involves no shortlisted credited name and no recusal is needed.
El-Manira discloses past co-authorship with Perlmann and notes that B012 lies in his own field, circuit neuroscience, with no documented tie to its credited names.
Sandberg notes that his RNA splicing work is topically near B028, which is not in his preferred configuration, and that topic proximity alone is not a conflict.
No member discloses a documented tie to any credited name on the shortlist, and no member requests recusal.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee support Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide on the record available, and if not, does the third place go to Knudsen or does the prize become a Holst and Drucker pair?
If the citation rests on physiology and the active peptide, how should it acknowledge the long-acting analogue step (Knudsen) without ruling on the Habener dispute?
Should the 2026 prize be a single achievement (B019 alone) or a split, and if split, which second part (B030, B040 or B012) and which B019 laureates would be dropped to stay within three people?
Does a fair three-person group exist for B012, and if so does it include Boyden or Bamberg? If not, does the committee treat B012 as ineligible for this year?
For B030, is the achievement CAR engineering (June, Sadelain) or adoptive cell therapy more broadly (with Rosenberg), and how should Eshhar's concept be handled?
Should a mechanism-led discovery with a clean pair of names (B040) outrank a therapy-linked candidate with unsettled credit (B030) as the second choice?
summary.chair_observation: The round-1 files show full convergence on one configuration, B019 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and no other ballot appears in any member's preferred configuration. The disagreement is in the choice of alternative (B030 for all six, B012 for three, B040 for three) and in how to settle the third GLP-1 place. Members flagged that unanimity at this stage may mask differing views on basic discovery versus drug development, which round 2 should address directly. Counts here come only from explicit statements in the six files.
